title: 2017 AMC 12A Problem 4
statement: Jerry and Silvia wanted to go from the southwest corner of a square field to the northeast corner. Jerry walked due east and then due north to reach the goal, but Silvia headed northeast and reached the goal walking in a straight line. Which of the following is closest to how much shorter Silvia’s trip was, compared to Jerry’s trip?

solutions.text:
If the square has side \(x,\) Jerry walks \(x+x=2x,\) while Silvia walks the diagonal \(\sqrt{x^2+x^2}=x\sqrt2.\)

The fraction by which Silvia’s trip is shorter is \[ \begin{aligned} &\dfrac{2x-x\sqrt2}{2x}=1-\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2} \\ &\approx 1-0.707=0.293. \end{aligned} \]

This is closest to \(30\%.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Let the side be \(x\); Jerry walks \(2x\) and Silvia walks the diagonal
The diagonal is \(x\sqrt2,\) so the fraction saved is \(\dfrac{2x-x\sqrt2}{2x}=1-\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\)
